Subject: Post-call: workload details & peak vs steady-state sizing for Acme Logistics

Hi Lisa — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the things we need to run a crisp sizing: 

- Short recap of the call: you’re planning to embed a conversational assistant into Acme’s driver app (customer-facing) and a separate internal routing assistant for ops. Primary constraints are tight P95 latency for driver flows and the ability to handle short bursts during shift changes.

- What would help us size conservatively:
  1) tokens per request: median & 95th (input + expected completion)
  2) desired latency SLOs (p50/p95; for streaming vs non-streaming flows)
  3) concurrency targets during steady-state and peak bursts (how many in-flight requests)
  4) QPS steady-state and peak burst QPS and typical burst duration
  5) whether streaming with partial token flushing is a hard requirement for driver flows

I attached a small throughput template (redwood-throughput-template.xlsx) you can drop numbers into — if you prefer, send a short CSV off the platform team and Dev will run a back-of-envelope.

Proposed short next steps:
- You fill the template (or paste numbers in reply) — Dev will produce a baseline sizing estimate and recommended SLA / concurrency knobs.
- We schedule a 45-min sizing workshop to walk through assumptions and runway for a spike environment.

Thanks — I’ll check back in Tuesday if I haven’t heard.

— Jordan

Lisa, Jordan — quick technical note based on the high-level call notes; happy to refine when you paste numbers. Below are conservative assumptions and a very small back-of-envelope for capacity planning.

Assumptions (example):
- average input tokens: 300
- average completion tokens: 150
- total tokens per request: 450
- target p95 latency (non-streaming): 150–200ms; streaming partial tokens allowed for driver flows -> lower perceived latency
- steady-state QPS: 35 (example)
- peak burst QPS: 220 for 3–5 minutes (example)
- concurrency = QPS * average latency (in seconds) as a baseline (e.g., if p95=0.15s, concurrency ~ QPS*0.15)

Back-of-envelope: tokens/sec = total_tokens_per_request * QPS
- steady tokens/sec = 450 * 35 = 15,750 tokens/sec
- peak tokens/sec = 450 * 220 = 99,000 tokens/sec

GPU sizing notes (very rough):
- On modern A100/V100-equivalent serving with batching and KV cache optimizations, a single well-utilized instance can sustain ~70k–120k tokens/sec for short sequences depending on quantization and model family.
- For the peak burst above (99k tokens/sec) we’d recommend planning for either 2x nodes with autoscale for burst or a dedicated burst pool to preserve latency SLOs.
- Streaming helps cut perceived latency and reduces strict p95 compute moments since partial tokens return earlier.

I attached a CSV with this simple calc so you can swap numbers. If you confirm p95 targets and whether streaming is required, I’ll produce a recommended cluster shape (node counts, target batch windows, warm KV cache strategy).

— Dev

Thanks Jordan/Dev — pasted the numbers below (filled from our analytics and a quick sample):

- Flow types: driver-facing conversational (short prompts, streaming desired) + internal ops chat (non-streaming ok)
- Average input tokens: 280 (driver), 420 (ops)
- Expected completion tokens: 120 (driver), 220 (ops)
- Total tokens per request (weighted): ~430
- Steady-state QPS (driver + ops combined): 28–38 (we see 35 as the 9am–4pm average)
- Peak burst QPS (shift changes + morning dispatch): 180–240, typical burst ~3–7 minutes
- Concurrency target (internal SLA): maintain p95 <= 150ms for driver streaming flows; for ops p95 <= 400ms is acceptable
- Streaming: driver flows require server-sent partial tokens; ops flows can be full-response

Other notes: we have strict security requirements — we’ll get the SOC2 questionnaire over the next week. Also, our procurement contact requested a cost-per-hour estimate for a short spike to validate UX.

If you can produce a short cluster recommendation and a ballpark spike estimate (1–2 hours) by EOD Wednesday that would be perfect. Thanks.
